solver.kind: blind AI solver B (separate agent, answer-free packet, adversarial rubric)

R054-01.notes: A states costs folded into rents, driving as default, and concludes builders' choice 'is how parking ought to be decided.' C is Passage B's view (trap); D contradicts 'Builders have not stopped providing parking'; A is unsupported.

R054-02.notes: Near-verbatim detail. A directly contradicted; B and D unsupported.

R054-03.notes: 'that cost is folded into rents and prices whether or not a tenant owns a car.' A (separate fee) is the opposite mechanism; B borrows Passage B's spillover idea.

R054-04.notes: 'in dense neighborhoods... I find it persuasive. But most Americans do not live in such places' plus the objection to 'eliminating minimums everywhere.' B and C are extremes; D is unsupported.

R054-05.notes: The line undercuts the assumption that no parking means no car ('the cars of its residents do not disappear'). C overstates (B never says residents are unwilling to use transit, only that service is infrequent); D runs against B's argument; A is unsupported.

R054-06.notes: Cars overflow and spread onto nearby blocks. 'Pour' is the literal-sense trap; it doesn't fit cars spreading across blocks well enough to be a second defensible answer.

R054-07.notes: Close paraphrase of B's 'A better approach would be...' sentence. B contradicts 'None of this means that the old rules should stay'; C is what B rejects; D is unsupported.

R054-08.notes: B says this outright ('Many codes demand far more spaces than buildings ever fill'). For A it is inferred: costs are charged regardless of car ownership, and builders chose less parking once free to decide, which implies required amounts exceeded demand. The inference is reasonable and no other option works: A is A's view only, B is contradicted by B, C is contradicted by A.

R054-09.notes: B's objection is spillover: residents' cars crowd nearby streets and hurt longtime neighbors, a cost the builder doesn't bear. B never says 'builders' outright, but C is the clear inference. A is an extreme the passage contradicts ('Many codes demand far more spaces than buildings ever fill' refers to codes, not builders' choices); B is irrelevant; D is unsupported.

R054-10.notes: 'Eliminating minimums everywhere at once trades one uniform rule for another' targets A's general endorsement of removal and leaving parking to builders. D (cities eliminated minimums) is a factual report, not the idea challenged; A and C are facts B doesn't dispute. A doesn't literally say 'every neighborhood', but its unqualified 'how parking ought to be decided' supports B, so this is not a second defensible answer.

R054-11.notes: 'The next Sunday I decided to find out' (whether he was letting her win or no longer seeing the board), then 'I kept my eyes on the board and waited.' A misreads the ending (she later loses, but that was not why she set the test); B and C are unsupported.
